thread:
nora: Heads-up: I made a tiny sample app to repro dupes when token rotates mid-retry. uses configurable jitter/backoff and can toggle auto-idempotency. dropping results here if anyone wants to eyeball.

jamal: nice. can you share the minimal cmd to run?

nora: sure:

```
./run_jitter_play.sh --rate 50 --duration 30 --token-rotate 0.75 --auto-key on --window-ms 500
```

kai: quick note: we should log server-assigned request_id and incoming Idempotency-Key to detect real duplicates vs resumed partial streams.

nora: done. also added a stream mode that attaches sequence numbers to each chunk. QA: can you run the smoke before noon?

qa-bot: test-run: jitter-smoke-2065005432 queued on staging.

jamal: one question on defaults: if auto-key is enabled, do we override user-provided Idempotency-Key? i think explicit header should always win.

kai: agreed. implement explicit wins and add a warning if key looks reused within process.

nora: initial results: auto-key+500ms window cut dup rate ~35% for non-stream; streams need extra seq dedupe. uploading logs to /staging/jitter-2065.zip

qa-bot: upload complete: /staging/jitter-2065.zip :white_check_mark:
thread_summary: short devex thread about a lightweight jitter/playground sample app to reproduce duplicates during token rotation and 429 bursts; discussed run command, logging request ids and idempotency keys, explicit-key precedence, and initial results
